results.name: between_set_yes_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation across sets (with at least 20 trials) of each set's overall yes rate; observed above null means people differ more between sets in overall willingness to generalize than the model predicts (model too homogeneous), below null means less.
results.code:
# name: between_set_yes_rate_sd
# description: Standard deviation across sets (with at least 20 trials) of each set's overall yes rate; observed above null means people differ more between sets in overall willingness to generalize than the model predicts (model too homogeneous), below null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    g = df.groupby("number_set")["rating"].agg(["mean", "size"])
    g = g[g["size"] >= 20]
    return float(g["mean"].std()) if len(g) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: late_session_yes_shift
results.description: Yes rate in the second half of the session (trial_index above median) minus the first half; observed below null means people become more conservative over the session than the stationary model predicts.
results.code:
# name: late_session_yes_shift
# description: Yes rate in the second half of the session (trial_index above median) minus the first half; observed below null means people become more conservative over the session than the stationary model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    late = ti > np.median(ti)
    return float(r[late].mean() - r[~late].mean())

results.name: partial_last_digit_match_effect
results.description: In multi-example sets whose examples do NOT all share a last digit, yes rate for targets sharing a last digit with at least one example minus yes rate for other targets; observed above null means people generalize by partial last-digit similarity more than the all-or-none rule model predicts.
results.code:
# name: partial_last_digit_match_effect
# description: In multi-example sets whose examples do NOT all share a last digit, yes rate for targets sharing a last digit with at least one example minus yes rate for other targets; observed above null means people generalize by partial last-digit similarity more than the all-or-none rule model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    ld = np.mod(ex, 10)
    first = ld[:, :1]
    same_all = np.all((ld == first) | np.isnan(ld), axis=1)
    sel = (n >= 2) & ~same_all & ~np.any(ex == t[:, None], axis=1)
    match = np.any(ld == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    a, b = sel & match, sel & ~match
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: single_example_far_yes_rate
results.description: For single-example sets, yes rate for targets more than 20 away from the example; observed above null means people generalize far from a lone example (via rules) more than the model predicts, below null means less.
results.code:
# name: single_example_far_yes_rate
# description: For single-example sets, yes rate for targets more than 20 away from the example; observed above null means people generalize far from a lone example (via rules) more than the model predicts, below null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    sel = (n == 1) & (np.abs(t - ex[:, 0]) > 20)
    return float(r[sel].mean()) if sel.any() else 0.0

results.name: wide_span_inside_hull_yes_rate
results.description: Among 3-4 example sets spanning at least 50 (max-min), yes rate for non-example targets lying inside [min,max]; observed above null means people generalize across the spanned range more than the model's interval/rule mixture predicts, below null means less.
results.code:
# name: wide_span_inside_hull_yes_rate
# description: Among 3-4 example sets spanning at least 50 (max-min), yes rate for non-example targets lying inside [min,max]; observed above null means people generalize across the spanned range more than the model's interval/rule mixture predicts, below null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo, hi = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    sel = (n >= 3) & (hi - lo >= 50) & (t >= lo) & (t <= hi) & ~np.any(ex == t[:, None], axis=1)
    return float(r[sel].mean()) if sel.any() else 0.0

results.name: target_in_set_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials whose target is one of the shown examples; observed below null means people reject shown examples more often than the model (which treats examples as near-certain members) predicts.
results.code:
# name: target_in_set_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate on trials whose target is one of the shown examples; observed below null means people reject shown examples more often than the model (which treats examples as near-certain members) predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    hit = np.any(ex == t[:, None], axis=1)
    return float(r[hit].mean()) if hit.any() else 0.0

results.name: last_vs_first_example_proximity
results.description: In 3-4 example sets, yes rate for non-example targets whose nearest example is the LAST shown minus those whose nearest is the FIRST shown; observed above null means a recency advantage the first-example-anchored model misses, below null means primacy stronger than modeled.
results.code:
# name: last_vs_first_example_proximity
# description: In 3-4 example sets, yes rate for non-example targets whose nearest example is the LAST shown minus those whose nearest is the FIRST shown; observed above null means a recency advantage the first-example-anchored model misses, below null means primacy stronger than modeled.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(ex - t[:, None])
    dist = np.where(np.isnan(dist), np.inf, dist)
    nearest = np.argmin(dist, axis=1)
    notex = ~np.any(ex == t[:, None], axis=1)
    sel = (n >= 3) & notex
    a = sel & (nearest == n - 1)
    b = sel & (nearest == 0)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: outside_hull_distance_slope
results.description: For targets outside the examples' [min,max] range, least-squares slope of yes (0/1) on log(1 + distance to nearest range edge); observed more negative than null means human generalization falls off with distance beyond the examples more steeply than the model predicts (less negative = flatter).
results.code:
# name: outside_hull_distance_slope
# description: For targets outside the examples' [min,max] range, least-squares slope of yes (0/1) on log(1 + distance to nearest range edge); observed more negative than null means human generalization falls off with distance beyond the examples more steeply than the model predicts (less negative = flatter).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo, hi = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    d = np.where(t < lo, lo - t, np.where(t > hi, t - hi, 0.0))
    sel = d > 0
    if sel.sum() < 3:
        return 0.0
    x = np.log1p(d[sel]); y = r[sel]
    vx = np.var(x)
    return float(np.mean((x - x.mean()) * (y - y.mean())) / vx) if vx > 0 else 0.0
